Triage: graded **Bug · `domain:devx` · `pm:blocked`** — this is the framework-side coordination card; the fix itself lands in objectui, where it is already filed and dispatched.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#5388

Rationale: objectui#5388 is precisely the remedy this card asks for (`assertLazyLinterStaysLazy` consuming `resolveSpecDistInjection`'s output instead of its private `SPEC` regex), in flight with the `repo:objectui` seat as of ~08:01Z today. Nothing in this repo can move until it lands **and** the pin can cover it; the named reader of this card is the `domain:devx` seat driving #10129 (the pin bump this blocks). ⛔ Per the card's own "not the remedy" section: no un-setting `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST`, no pinning below `6d5368ac8` without a maintainer call — if #10129's dev needs an interim pin decision before objectui#5388 lands, that goes to the decision box, not into the PR.

Unlock-action: when objectui#5388 merges, re-verify the repro (`bash scripts/build-console.sh` against a pin at/after the fix) and return this to #10129's path rather than re-dispatching separately.

**Fixed upstream and confirmed here.** Closing.

The fix landed as **objectui#5390** — verified by content on objectui `origin/main` (`9a3daf8d37ad973a`), not by sha ancestry:

- `apps/console/vite.config.ts:98` — `assertLazyLinterStaysLazy(specTest: RegExp)` now takes the spec test as a parameter
- `:435` — registered as `assertLazyLinterStaysLazy(specModuleTest)`
- `:414–415` — `specModuleTest` comes from the injection when `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST` is set
- `scripts/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.ts:271` — the producer publishes `specModuleTest: widen(specModuleTest)` beside `vendorChunkTest`, from one shared `widen()` so the two cannot drift apart again

This card argued the fix belonged upstream and should read the producer's output rather than widen a tolerance locally. That is what landed. Worth recording that the obvious shortcut was rejected on measurement: feeding the probe the existing `vendorChunkTest` would have turned the build green, but that test is the whole `@objectstack` vendor scope **minus** the linter, so an eager `@objectstack/client` would have satisfied a probe whose entire job is to prove the walk can see the **spec**. Green by lowering the bar, and it would have looked like a fix.

**Confirmed on this side, not assumed:** #10137 bumped `.objectui-sha` to `9a3daf8d37ad973a` and **Console Pin Gate passed** (run [`32351515723`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/32351515723), job completed 09:07:41). That is the same `bash scripts/build-console.sh` that failed here with `counter-probe failed: no eagerly loaded chunk contains an @objectstack/spec module`. The pin is on `main` now, so the failing condition is not merely avoided — it is exercised and green.

**The `LINT` half this card flagged is handled, deliberately and differently.** objectui#5390 did *not* make `LINT` injection-aware — nothing injects `@objectstack/lint` today, so there is no producer to read and inventing one would be speculative and untestable. Instead that half gained its own counter-probe, on an asymmetry worth keeping in mind: a blind **spec** test fails **loud** (this bug), a blind **lint** test fails **silent**, because the assertion on it is negative and zero matches is indistinguishable from "the linter is properly lazy" while ~89 KiB gzipped ships on every page load. So if #9659's proposal to inject four more `@objectstack/*` packages lands and lint joins the set, the probe says so rather than quietly ceasing to guard anything.

Related finding left open: objectui#5391 — `resolveSpecDistInjection` validates the override's exports targets but not that the overriding package's own dependencies resolve from its location, so a dep-less spec dist fails ~80 s later as a rolldown `failed to resolve zod`, naming zod rather than `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST`.
